chef.title: Julien Marchetti
chef.subtitle: Executive Chef & Founder
paragraphs: Julien cooks seasonal Lowcountry food with French technique: shrimp from Shem Creek, greens from Johns Island and sauces made the slow way. His menus are generous rather than fussy, built around what is best that week and the people at your table.
He still cooks most Savrio dinners himself, and he calls every host before a menu is written.

items.question: How much does a private chef dinner cost?
items.answer: It depends on the menu, the number of guests and the service you need. Most of our dinner parties fall between $95 and $160 per guest, including the chef, groceries, service and clean-up. Wine pairings and the mobile bar are quoted separately.

items.question: Can you cook for allergies and dietary needs?
items.answer: Absolutely. We ask about every guest’s allergies and preferences when we plan the menu, and we cook gluten-free, dairy-free, vegetarian, vegan and nut-free dishes as carefully as everything else.

items.question: How far ahead should we book?
items.answer: Two to four weeks is usually enough for a dinner party. For weddings, holidays and Saturdays in spring and autumn, we recommend booking three to six months ahead.

items.question: Is my kitchen big enough?
items.answer: In almost every case, yes. We’ve cooked in galley kitchens, beach rentals and barns. For larger events we bring portable induction, ovens and our own equipment.

items.question: Do you bring plates, glassware and staff?
items.answer: We can. Every quote can include servers, bartenders, plates, cutlery, linens and glassware, or we’ll happily use your own china for a more personal table.

items.question: What about the leftovers?
items.answer: They’re yours. We portion, label and refrigerate anything left over before we leave, so tomorrow’s lunch is taken care of too — nothing goes to waste.
